title: The whole-litre rounding gap
hook: 250mL per cup can leave a whole-litre fill above the exact requirement.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Compute excess created by rounding a volume to coarse increments.

misconception: A rounded fill volume always equals the exact serving volume.
objective: Compute excess created by rounding a volume to coarse increments.

claims.text: Each empty cup is allocated 250mL. Compare exact total volume with that total rounded up to whole litres. Scaled model; empty cups; volume only; no heating guidance.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Cups=5, A=1.25L and B=2L. The geometry pictures follow the declared dimension relationships; other stage pictures are scaled to the larger displayed comparison and icons are not literal item counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/",["*","x",250],1000]; B=["ceil",["/",["*","x",250],1000]]; x denotes Cups. At x=5, A=1.25, B=2; recall at x=8: B=2. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

claims.text: Multiply cup count by millilitres per cup, then convert to litres. Rounding up introduces an excess that is visible as the difference between the two results. Exact need and a coarse fill increment are different quantities.

recall.question: Each empty cup is allocated 250mL. Compare exact total volume with that total rounded up to whole litres. Change only Cups to 8. What is B (Whole-litres) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Cups=8: it gives 2L. Multiply cup count by millilitres per cup, then convert to litres. Rounding up introduces an excess that is visible as the difference between the two results. Exact need and a coarse fill increment are different quantities.
